English සිංහල தமிழ் Fact Checked All Economy Society Environment Politics Health Methodology About Us Explore Fact-Checking Contact Us #false False Claims of Dam Break Risks at Victoria, Moragahakanda and Kotmale Reservoirs False Social media claims that dams at Victoria, Moragahakanda and Kotmale reservoirs were at risk are false. Officials and the Disaster Management Centre confirmed there was no danger. by Anonymous | December 1, 2025 News circulating on social media claimed that dams at the Moragahakanda , Victoria and Kotmale reservoirs were at risk of breaking due to the prevailing bad weather. The rumours caused panic among residents, prompting some to leave their homes. https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Cuf6axxWt/ FactSeeker investigated these claims and confirmed through government officials that the information was false. Officials stated that only 80 cubic meters of water per second had been released on the relevant days and that there was no risk of any structural failure. https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1DC12BDZ11/ The Disaster Management Centre also issued an official statement confirming that there was no danger to any of the dams at Victoria, Moragahakanda or Kotmale. Several media outlets reported the same clarification. https://srilankamirror.com/news/reservoir-dams-have-not-breached-disaster-management-centre/?hl=en-GB&amp=1 https://hirunews.lk/433549/there-is-no-risk-of-moragahakanda-and-kotmale-dams-breaking-dmc?hl=en-GB Accordingly, FactSeeker confirms that the social media posts claiming these dams were at risk of breaching are false. We are an independent fact-checking team affiliated with the Sri Lanka Press Institute(SLPI). The objective and long-term goal of the FactSeeker is to provide the public with reliable and verified content in the attempt of debunking mis/disinformation. The unit, with the SLPI, is committed to contributing to improved media literacy in Sri Lanka.
